claims.text: The target material is a Ta-based BCC refractory high-entropy alloy initially present as a disordered solid solution.
Standard experimental measurements of melting properties are infeasible for the target alloys.
Ab initio free-energy calculations using full thermodynamic integration are computationally prohibitive for the target alloys.
Empirical EAM potentials fail to capture the complex liquid structure of multicomponent refractory alloys.
Machine-learning models using Holder means of elemental properties and structural properties can predict shear and bulk moduli of NbTaTiV with relatively small errors.
The demonstrated success of such descriptors for elastic moduli implies that an MLP using them can efficiently approximate the high-temperature solid and liquid free-energy landscape.
Replacing full thermodynamic integration with the proposed MLP perturbation scheme will produce free-energy estimates within 5% of ab initio benchmarks.
The proposed MLP perturbation scheme will reduce computational cost by more than 90% relative to full ab initio thermodynamic integration.
Ta-Cr has a positive enthalpy of mixing that drives phase separation and Laves-phase precipitation.
Ta-Cr cross-interactions can promote Cr2Ta Laves-phase formation and reduce BCC-phase stability in a Ta-containing refractory HEA.
Accurately learning Ta-Cr cross-interactions is necessary to reproduce liquid short-range order and local atomic environments.
If the training set lacks configurations representing the relevant mixing energetics, the MLP will artifactually stabilize the disordered phase.
Artifactually stabilizing the disordered phase will overestimate solid-solution stability and underestimate the free-energy difference between solid and liquid phases.
A machine-learning model trained on ordered compounds may lose accuracy when applied to a disordered HEA because lattice distortion is not fully represented in its training data.
The cited evidence establishes that ordered-compound training may fail specifically for the disordered liquid state at temperatures near melting.
The quality and completeness of the underlying data strongly affect the accuracy of thermodynamic predictions.
At high temperature, an ordered-only MLP will predict a stable single-phase BCC state in cases where a liquid-augmented MLP and ab initio or experimental results show significant Laves precipitation.
Agreement of the liquid-augmented MLP with ab initio free energies within 5%, together with a speedup greater than tenfold, would support the claimed efficiency gain.
